claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature and near 1000 °C.
Ta should be entirely replaced by Nb to form HfMoNbTiZr.
Replacing Ta with Nb will reduce alloy density by more than approximately 10% relative to 10.21 g/cm³.
HfMoNbTiZr will maintain yield strength, tensile strength, and creep resistance similar to HfMoTaTiZr from room temperature to approximately 1000 °C.
The Nb-substituted alloy will retain a similar single-phase BCC or related microstructure.
The Nb-substituted alloy will retain lattice distortion comparable to that of HfMoTaTiZr.
Ta is the densest component of HfMoTaTiZr, and Nb has a significantly lower density than Ta.
Nb provides refractory behavior comparable to Ta.
The similar chemical nature and atomic size of Nb and Ta will preserve solid-solution strengthening and lattice-distortion strengthening.
The proposed performance envelope includes tensile, compressive, and creep loading from room temperature to approximately 1000 °C.
The expected outcome is limited to as-cast material produced with cooling conditions similar to those of the baseline.
Processing-induced phase or microstructural changes outside the stated conditions may alter mechanical performance.
Nb substitution may change phase stability or microstructure and thereby subtly affect mechanical properties.
Matched HfMoTaTiZr and HfMoNbTiZr batches can be compared using density measurement, XRD, microscopy, and room- and high-temperature mechanical testing.
The hypothesis is rejected if density decreases by less than approximately 10% or if yield or tensile strength falls by more than approximately 15% at room temperature or approximately 1000 °C.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says mechanical properties will be preserved or not sacrificed, but the rejection rule permits decreases of up to approximately 15% in yield or tensile strength. Thus, an appreciable strength sacrifice could still be counted as confirmation.
